references.text: Caleb, son of Jephunneh, is mentioned as the spy from the tribe of Judah who was sent to explore the land.
Hoshea (Joshua), son of Nun, is mentioned as the spy from the tribe of Ephraim.
Moses gave Hoshea, son of Nun, the name Joshua.
Caleb showed faith by encouraging the people to take possession of the land, unlike the other spies.
Joshua and Caleb tore their clothes and spoke against the people's rebellion, showing their trust in the Lord's promise.
The Lord promised that Caleb would be allowed to enter the land because of his faithfulness.
Only Caleb and Joshua from that generation were allowed to enter the Promised Land.
It confirms that Caleb, son of Jephunneh, and Joshua, son of Nun, were the only survivors among those who were numbered in the wilderness of Sinai.
Caleb and Joshua are mentioned as the only ones who followed the Lord wholeheartedly.
Moses reminds that only Caleb and Joshua would be allowed to see the Promised Land because of their faithfulness.
Caleb receives his inheritance in Hebron as a reward for his faithfulness when he spied out the land.
The book of Hebrews refers to the rebellion in the wilderness and how most were not allowed to enter into rest because of unbelief, while Joshua and Caleb were spared.
